practices.summary: A GSI whose partition key duplicates the table's adds no new access pattern - index it only when it changes sort key or projection intentionally.
GSI partition keys on low-cardinality attributes (status/type/flag) concentrate index traffic on few partitions.
GSI reads are always eventually consistent; ConsistentRead is rejected on index queries.
LSIs can only be created at table creation time and share the table's partition key; 10 GB item-collection limit applies.
Provisioned indexes with no observed access path are dead capacity; accesses naming undeclared indexes fail at runtime.
